scenes.title: Cover
scenes.text: Every school should observe lessons. Very few can show what happens next. This is the Observation System: one route from lesson observation, to collected evidence, to a coaching plan for every teacher, covering every step of the learning journey. Here is the whole journey.

scenes.title: The form
scenes.text: It starts in the classroom. The teacher coach opens one form and fills in the observation details: subject, class and teacher, with live dropdowns fed by the school's own staff directory, so nothing is typed from memory and no list is ever out of date. Class composition is a few taps. The whole context of the lesson, captured throughout the observation.

scenes.title: The regulator's scale
scenes.text: Each observation uses the Regulatory Body's own six point scale, from Very Weak to Outstanding, with the same proportion bands its inspectors already use. Ten criteria, from attainment and progress to teaching and leadership, each with room for a comment. The form speaks the language of inspection, because it was built to coach teachers using the same criteria.

scenes.title: Evidence Pad
scenes.text: Coaching notes can be handwritten. The form has an Evidence Pad, designed for Apple Pencil. The observer types, or writes with the Pencil, and keeps photos of the board or the pupils' work alongside. The system reads the handwriting and turns it into text. Everything is saved automatically throughout the observation, so nothing is ever lost mid lesson.

scenes.title: Save and Lock
scenes.text: When it is done, each observation gets its own ID, freezes, and everything is saved, ready for review.

scenes.title: One tap, filed four ways
scenes.text: One tap files everything, four ways at once. The observation lands in a spreadsheet. It mirrors into a live database, duplicate proof by design. A branded backup email goes to the observer, for safe keeping and easy access, with a link to the locked observation. And the handwriting itself is archived in private storage, so it can be reviewed if ever needed.

scenes.title: The dashboard story
scenes.text: Now the other end of the pipeline. The Observation Dashboard opens with a password, safety as a priority. As an example, here is one school's June round. The story plays itself: a hundred and eleven lessons, a hundred and five teachers, counted up live from the data. Where judgements sit on the six point scale. What is working. Where to focus next. And one tap presents that round's findings in full screen, built to showcase the round by itself in any meeting.

scenes.title: Evidence behind every claim
scenes.text: Every written statement carries a small number: a citation, a reference stemming from an actual observation. Click or tap to open the references and see the actual observations behind each statement: subject, date, judgement, and the inspector's words, verbatim. AI cites the hundreds of references that sit behind every claimed statement. Nothing on this dashboard is an opinion without evidence.

scenes.title: Movement between rounds
scenes.text: Rounds can be compared to show movement. Every teacher seen in both rounds is displayed as a line, from where they were to where they are, green when they moved toward Outstanding. A transition matrix counts the improvements, the holds and the declines. This is the question governors actually ask: is teaching getting better? If not, why? And how can we improve?

scenes.title: Coverage
scenes.text: The Dashboard shows Coverage, which answers the other question: who has been seen? Teachers on the register, teachers observed, lessons per teacher, and who is still waiting, so no one is invisible for a term.

scenes.title: The teacher view
scenes.text: Drill into any teacher and their history follows. Two gauges, student progress and teaching, averaged across every observation. Each session, its skills and its notes, one card each. And below them, a coaching plan: drafted by AI from that teacher's own lessons, checked word for word against the source, grounded in the school's own rubric, then amended if needed and approved by the teacher coach before the teacher ever sees it.

scenes.title: The teacher portal
scenes.text: Teachers have their own door. A portal for every member of staff: their photograph, their history, and a notification when a new coaching plan is approved. What they see is deliberately thinner than what leadership sees. No observer's rough notes, no edits, no other teachers, only their own approved coaching plan and their own next steps.

scenes.title: Reports and regeneration
scenes.text: For the leadership table, one button turns the round into a governance report, simple or in depth, and a second builds it as a branded Google Doc, all references attached, teachers anonymised by construction. When a new round lands, one more button rewrites the analysis for it, the AI's work double checked by the Head of Teaching and Learning before publishing.

scenes.title: Trust
scenes.text: Underneath, three locks. A password for the school. A second, server verified password for administrators. And a unique key for every single entry. The whole system runs on the tools a school already pays for: Google Workspace, a database, and static hosting. No servers to maintain, no per seat licences, and the data stays in accounts the school controls.

scenes.title: Close
scenes.text: From a lesson observed, to evidence, to a plan in the teacher's hand. One system, built inside a school, ready to travel. Better never stops.
